description_full: Nutanix, Inc. provides a cloud and artificial intelligence platform (AI) in North America, Europe, the Asia Pacific, the Middle East, Latin America, and Africa. It offers hyperconverged infrastructure software (HCI); Nutanix Cloud Platform for building hybrid multicloud infrastructure; Nutanix cloud infrastructure, a distributed HCI for enterprise IT applications, including Nutanix AOS, Nutanix AHV, Nutanix data services for Kubernetes, flow network security, flow virtual networking, Nutanix Cloud Clusters, Nutanix central, and Nutanix prism; and Nutanix Cloud Manager, is a unified management solution, such as NCM Intelligent Operations, NCM Self-Service and Orchestration, NCM Cost Governance, and Nutanix Security Central unifies cloud security operations. The company also offers Nutanix Kubernetes Platform, an enterprise Kubernetes platform for deploying and managing modern, containerized applications across hybrid multicloud environments; Nutanix Enterprise AI, a centralized fine-tuning and inferencing platform; Nutanix Agent Gateway for governing interactions between agents, LLMs, and tools; Nutanix Private Inferencing that helps organizations to build adaptive AI factories; Nutanix Unified Storage, a software-defined platform that consolidates file, object, and block storage into one intelligent data fabric; Nutanix Files Storage, a software-defined scale-out file storage solution; Nutanix Objects Storage, a scale-out S3-compatible object storage solution; Nutanix Volumes Block Storage, a software-defined storage solution; and Nutanix Data Lens, a cloud-based cyber resilience service. In addition, it provides product support, and consulting and implementation services. The company serves financial services, retail, manufacturing, public sector, automotive and other transportation, consumer goods, education, energy, healthcare, media, technology, and telecommunications industries. The company was incorporated in 2009 and is headquartered in San Jose, California.

financial_summary: Nutanix, Inc. is a large-cap technology business with a $15.9B market cap on $2.9B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +15% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder. Operating margins are expanding by +7.3pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Gross margins of 79% are the starting point for assessing pricing power.

The business throws off $841M in free cash flow — roughly 29 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders. Cash conversion is thin at 0.61×, however, which raises the oldest question in analysis: are these earnings backed by cash?.
Accruals are elevated at +11.6% of assets, and Sloan showed firms building earnings through accruals rather than cash systematically underperform.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 40× is fortress-like.

Shareholder yield of 3.0% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and stock-based comp at 13% of revenue is silent dilution an owner has to account for, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome, and profit capture is only 0.4× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.

sect: Its 10% operating margin is roughly in line with the Technology median (7%).
It captures well under its share of sector profits (0.41x its revenue share).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.03 across 530 companies in the universe; the top four hold 29% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares have drifted higher, up 7% over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 23% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 47% and a beta of 1.05, it moves roughly with the market.
Liquidity is deep, with about $159.2M traded a day.
In past sell-offs it fell 67% in the 2020 crash and 57% in the 2022 bear market.
val: The price sits above its DCF fair value of $38.25 (margin of safety -53%), so there is no valuation cushion.
Multiples send mixed signals against Technology peers: cheaper on P/E 11.3 vs 26.7 and P/FCF 18.9 vs 25.4, richer on EV/EBITDA 40.4 vs 16.4 (sector median).
Earnings yields are mixed: an FCF yield of 5.3% (above the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 1.8% (vs the 8% bar).
The 15 covering analysts target $79.27 on average, 36% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
The price implies 24.7% annual cash-flow growth, 10pp more than the model expects.
prof: It runs a 79% gross margin and converts 29% of revenue into free cash flow, or 17% after stock compensation.
Earnings quality is a concern: a weak Piotroski score of 3/9, cash conversion of only 0.61x and high accruals (+11.6% of assets).
ROE of 214% is amplified by 7.2x balance-sheet leverage (DuPont), so ROIC is the cleaner read on the business.
Operating margin is running 36pp above its own historical average, a peak-margin risk if conditions normalise.
It spends 27.7% of revenue on R&D and 12.5% on stock compensation (above the 2% gate).
hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $2.4B (5% of market cap).
Warning signs: a Beneish M-score that flags possible earnings manipulation, which caps the rating at HOLD.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 15.3% over 3 years and 15.4% over 5 years, and it has been lumpy (year-to-year swings of 13%).
Capex roughly matches depreciation (1.1x, 2.7% of sales), a maintenance pace.
Its Rule of 40 score is 32, below the 40 that marks a healthy growth business.
It has beaten earnings estimates by 21.5% on average.
own: Insiders own a modest 1.8%, and institutions hold 96%.
Insiders have only sold over the past year (11 sales, net $57.2M sold).
It returns 3.0% a year to shareholders (3.0% in buybacks).
The share count has grown 7.3% a year over five years, diluting existing holders.
people: With about 8,350 employees, each generates about $342K of revenue, in line with the Technology median, and productivity has risen 15.7% a year.
That works out to $101K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $1.6M (5x revenue per employee), and compensation governance scores well (3/10, lower is better).
